facts.value: Method II: net wages = wages - Table A allowance for the payroll period; apply the per-period table (weekly/biweekly/semimonthly/monthly/daily) or the Annual Tax Rate Schedule for annual payrolls: (net - col3) x col4 + col5. Annualised net wages (net x payroll periods) are used only to test the Method III threshold. Other periods: convert via a factor to a common period, apply its table, convert the result back (p.23).
facts.authority: NY Department of Taxation and Finance
facts.note: The publication does not instruct annualising wages for Method II. Observation (G-DERIVE, not a rule): per-period tables = annual schedule / periods with floors rounded to whole dollars (weekly line 2: 8,500/52 = 163.46 -> 163; base 332/52 = 6.38), so annualise-and-divide gives near but not identical results.

facts.value: Method III: annualized wages = Method II net wages x payroll periods per year (e.g. 52, 26, 24, 12); x column 3 rate; / payroll periods = amount to withhold.

facts.value: Nothing withheld unless weekly disposable earnings exceed the GREATER of 30x the federal minimum hourly wage or 30x the state minimum hourly wage in Labor Law 652 (so the state minimum applies when higher); cap is the lesser of 25% of disposable earnings or the excess over that floor; 10% of gross for the 10% execution. The clause as read does not name a Labor Law 652 region

facts.value: Timing is statutory: Labor Law 590(2) requires the written notice at the time of each permanent or indefinite separation, reduction in hours, temporary separation and other interruption causing total or partial unemployment. DOL page (A.2): notice required for employees whose hours drop to 30 or less per week or who go off payroll; content: employer name, registration number, FEIN, payroll-records mailing address, claim instructions. The 12 NYCRR 472.8 text itself was not read (govt.westlaw.com not tried); dol.ny.gov/notice-eligibility-ui-benefits still returns Access denied (not bypassed).
